integrations.label: Connects to the platforms you already sell and ship on

problem.headline: Most operational work is copying data between systems.
problem.body: Webshop, warehouse, marketplaces, accounting, spreadsheets. Each does its job. None of them talk to each other, so your team bridges the gap by hand.

items.title: Double entry
items.body: The same order or product is typed into two or three systems. Every entry is a chance for a mismatch.

items.title: Stock out of sync
items.body: An item sells in one channel and stays live in another. The second buyer gets a cancellation.

items.title: Spreadsheets as glue
items.body: Exports downloaded, cleaned and re-uploaded on a schedule someone has to remember.

items.title: Silent failures
items.body: An import stops or a file never arrives, and the gap surfaces days later in a report.

services.headline: The work between a sale and a closed book.
services.body: Six automations we build most often. Each runs on a schedule or a webhook, logs what it did, and asks for a person only when it needs one.

items.title: Inventory sync
items.body: Stock levels checked across every channel. Sold-out items paused everywhere, automatically.

items.title: Order routing
items.body: Orders pulled from marketplaces and webshops, matched to the right variant, created in your warehouse or ERP.

items.title: Record matching
items.body: Products, variants and customers reconciled across systems by code, name and attributes. Matched once, reused forever.

items.title: Reports and exports
items.body: Stock, sales and exception reports delivered to Sheets, Excel or email, in the layout your team already uses.

items.title: Documents and finance
items.body: Invoices, credit notes and payment updates generated from orders and booked into accounting.

items.title: Retries, logs, alerts
items.body: Rate limits, outages and bad data handled with backoff. Every action logged. Dry-run before anything changes.

process.headline: From first call to running automation.

steps.title: Audit
steps.body: A 30-minute call. We map your systems and the data that moves between them. You get a written scope and a fixed quote.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: We connect the APIs, reconcile your data and run everything in dry-run next to your team. You see each action before it happens.

steps.title: Go live
steps.body: Dry-run off. Orders, stock and documents move on their own. Alerts go to the channel your team already watches.

steps.title: Operate
steps.body: We monitor runs, absorb API changes and add automations as the operation grows.

work.headline: Automation underneath. AI on top.
work.body: Two recent builds: the plumbing that keeps a multi-channel retailer's stock and orders in sync, and an AI sales agent that sells inside the chat apps customers already use.

ops.label: Operations automation
ops.title: A retailer selling through a warehouse, a webshop and two marketplace regions.
before: Sold-out listings paused by hand after each sale

ai.label: AI sales agent
ai.title: A sales agent that answers, finds the product and closes the order inside the chat.
ai.body: Built for a social-commerce store on Messenger, WhatsApp and Instagram. The agent understands the customer's language, matches photos to products, collects the order and books the courier. A human takes over with one click.

chat.text: Do you have this one in 42?

Order #1042 placed. Courier booked, arrives tomorrow. Tracking link sent.

caps.title: Social sales agent
caps.body: Messenger, WhatsApp and Instagram in one inbox, with human handoff.

caps.title: Shopify sales agent
caps.body: The same agent on your Shopify store: answers, recommends, converts.

caps.title: AI visual search
caps.body: Customer sends a photo, gets the matching product and size.

caps.title: Similar-product recommendations
caps.body: Every reply shows the next best options, which lifts basket size.

items.q: Do we have to change the systems we use?
items.a: No. Coelor connects to what you already run through its API. If a system has no API, we work from its exports.

items.q: What kind of work can be automated?
items.a: Anything that follows rules and moves data between systems: orders, stock, invoices, reports, customer records, notifications.

items.q: What happens when one of our systems goes down?
items.a: Runs retry with backoff and resume where they stopped. Nothing is applied twice. You get an alert if a run fails twice in a row.

items.q: Can we see what it will do before it changes anything?
items.a: Yes. Every automation ships with a dry-run mode that logs each action it would take without taking it.

items.q: How long until it is live?
items.a: Most builds take 3 to 6 weeks from the audit call, depending on how many systems are involved.
You do. It runs in your cloud account or ours, with documentation and handover included.
